contexts.text: See Leah. AC 422. AC 3902.
How the good of truth was conjoined with related good... afterwards by the affection of internal truth, which is Rachel. Treated of.
Behold, Rachel his daughter () = the affection of interior truth.
Rachel came with the flock () = the affection of interior truth which is of the Church and of doctrine.
That Rachel represents the affection of interior truth. Explained.
These are the things represented by Jacob, and by his two wives, Rachel and Leah. Fully explained.

Rachel, therefore, now puts on the representation of truth; but, as all the conjunction of truth with good is effected through affection, it is the affection of truth to be coupled with good, which Rachel represents. Moreover, in the Natural... there is an interior and an exterior; and Rachel represents the affection of interior truth; and Leah, the affection of exterior truth. Laban, who was their father, represents collateral good... Hence the daughters from this good, represent affections in the Natural... And, as these affections are to be coupled with natural good, they represent affections of truth... The case with the regeneration of man as to his natural, is altogether the same as it was with Jacob and the two daughters of Laban, Rachel and Leah.

For she was a shepherdess... () = that the affection of interior truth teaches what is in the Word... The reason it is from the Word, is that Rachel came to the well with her flock. Moreover, it is the affection of interior truth which teaches.
When Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother () = the acknowledgement of the affection of that truth, from what origin it was. Explained.
Jacob kissed Rachel () = love towards interior truths.
Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother () = the affinity of the (two goods); and Rachel, to whom this was made known, = the affection of interior truth.
She ran, and told her father () = acknowledgement through interior truths... That it was through interior truths, is represented by Rachel, who is the affection of interior truth. Explained.
The name of the younger was Rachel () = the affection of internal truth, with its quality.
Rachel is called the younger, because internal truth is learned afterwards. (Continued. See Leah.)

When general ideas have been illustrated by singulars, they become firm and steadfast; for they have thence things essential and formal, which are signified by the beautiful form and aspect of Rachel; by whom are represented the affections of interior truth. Example(s). AC 3821.
Jacob loved Rachel () = the love of good towards internal truth; (for) Rachel = the affection of internal truth; here, internal truth to be conjoined with the good of the Natural.
He said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter () = study, and a holy state then, that he might be conjoined with internal truth. Explained. AC 3826.
Laban said, It is better that I should give her to thee... () = a medium of conjunction through interior truth with that good. Rachel = interior truth. Explained.
They were... as a few days, in his love for her () = a state of love. Explained.
Give me my woman () = ... conjunction now with the affection of interior truth; (which is represented) by Rachel, who is here my woman.
Have I not served with thee for Rachel () = that the study had been for the affection of internal truth.
(It is not so done) to give the younger before the first-born () = (that the state is not such) that the affection of interior truth should precede the affection of external truth. Explained.
He gave him Rachel his daughter for a woman () = the conjunction then of good with the affection of interior truth. Explained. AC 3850.
He loved Rachel more than Leah () = the love of internal truth more than for external.
Rachel was barren () = that interior truths were not received. Explained.
Rachel saw that she did not bear... () = that interior truth was not yet acknowledged. Rachel = the affection of interior truth, or interior truth [itself].
Rachel was zealous against her sister () = indignation that interior truth was not acknowledged as external truth was.
She said to Jacob, Give me sons () = that she wanted to have interior truths from the truth of natural good.
Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel ()... = that the interior truth represented by Rachel could not as yet be acknowledged in faith and act by the good of the natural.
The mediums on the side of the internal man, are signified by the handmaids of Rachel.
She shall bear upon my knees () = the acknowledgement of the interior truth represented by Rachel. Explained.
Rachel said, God hath judged me, and hath also heard my voice () = justice and mercy; the Holy of faith; and the good of life. Explained.
Rachel said, With the wrestlings of God have I wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed () = Own power; temptation in which one overcomes; and resistance by the natural man. Explained.
Rachel = the affection of the internal man.
Rachel said to Leah () = the perception of the affection of interior truth, and the longing of it. AC 3945. AC 3952:3. Explained. AC 3952:5.
God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her () = foresight and Providence.
And opened her womb () = the faculty to receive and acknowledge... the goods of truth, and the truths of good.

She said, God hath gathered up my reproach; and she called his name Joseph, saying, Jehovah add to me another son () = the Lord as to the Divine Spiritual; the Spiritual Kingdom, or good of faith; and salvation with fructification and multiplication... For (these words) = that Rachel was no longer barren, nor dead; for by Rachel is represented the affection of interior truth; or the interior man as to truth; and the interior man is as it were dead as to truth and good, if the exterior man does not correspond to it in respect to goods and truths. Explained.
When Rachel had borne Joseph () = the acknowledgement of the Spiritual (through) the affection of interior truth. Explained.

Jacob... called Rachel and Leah to the field unto his flock () = the adjunction of the affections of truth by the good of the Natural... Rachel = the affection of interior truth... The flock = the goods and truths themselves which have now been acquired, and to which the affections of truth meant by Rachel and Leah were applied...

Rachel and Leah answered... () = the reciprocal of the affections of truth... Rachel = the affection of interior truth... The subject just treated of, is how the good of the natural adjoined to itself the affections of truth which are signified by Rachel and Leah; and the subject now, is the reciprocal application to good of these affections of truth.
(The separation of the affections of truth represented by Rachel and Leah from the good signified by Laban.) Treated of.

Lest thou shouldst take thy daughters from me by force () = that this good would be injured in respect to the affections of truth... for by daughters, here, Rachel and Leah, are signified affections of truth. AC 4177. AC 4185. AC 4200.
Rachel stealing the gods. Explained.
Rachel = the affection of interior truth. AC 4343.
As the truths represented by the gods were internal, they were found in the tent of Rachel, that is, in the Holy of the affection of interior truth. AC 4154. AC 4155.
He divided the sons over to Rachel () = the disposition of interior truth under their own affection.
He placed... Rachel and Joseph hindermost () = ... the affection of interior truth (which) is still more interior; (and thus more particular). Explained. AC 4362.
Rachel brought forth, and suffered hard things... () = the temptations of interior truth.
Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath () = the end of the former affection of interior truth... and the resuscitation of a new state [of it]. AC 6243.

The sons of Rachel: Joseph, and Benjamin () = interior goods and truths; (for) Rachel = the affection of interior truth; thus the sons of Rachel = interior goods and truths. Enumerated. AC 5469. AC 5826.
The sons of Rachel the wife of Jacob () = the things which are from celestial affection. AC 6024:5.
Whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel () = from the affection of internal good.
How Rachel represented the new Church. (Explained.)
Rachel represents the Church as to good; but... the Internal Church. (See Leah.)
Rachel wrestling with her sister, and prevailing = that the spiritual man fought with the natural. Explained.

Rachel weeping for her sons, refuseth to be comforted for her sons, because there was not any ()... Rachel represented the Internal Spiritual Church (and the above words = ) that no spiritual truth remained. (The succeeding words explained.)
